items.stem: AI drafts a variance commentary attributing a cost rise to 'higher volume'. The data shows flat volume and a price increase. What should the analyst do?

options.text: Correct the narrative to the real driver after checking the figures
options.rationale: Correct: AI commentary must be verified against the data before use.

options.text: Publish the AI narrative as written to save time
options.rationale: Publishing an unverified, wrong driver misleads decision-makers.

options.text: Trust the AI because it is confident
options.rationale: Confident wording is not evidence of accuracy.

options.text: Remove all commentary to avoid risk
options.rationale: The fix is verification and correction, not omission.

items.explanation: Correct: AI commentary must be verified against the data before use.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO data risks most directly undermine AI-assisted FP&A analysis? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Poor data quality in the inputs
options.rationale: Correct: AI amplifies errors in low-quality input data.

options.text: Entering confidential financials into an uncontrolled tool
options.rationale: Correct: this creates confidentiality and control risks.

options.text: Using a clearly labelled chart of accounts
options.rationale: A clean chart of accounts helps rather than harms analysis.
Reconciliation improves reliability; it is not a risk.

items.stem: Why should an AI point forecast not be presented to the CFO as a single certain number?

options.text: Forecasts carry uncertainty; a range and assumptions communicate risk honestly
options.rationale: Correct: presenting uncertainty and assumptions is more truthful and useful than a false-precision point.

options.text: AI forecasts are always wrong and should be hidden
options.rationale: AI can assist forecasting; the issue is representing uncertainty, not hiding output.

options.text: A single number is always more accurate
options.rationale: A single number hides the uncertainty that exists.
